reason: A before/after loopback latency proof for one workload: it measures rather than decides, and its budget only runs when the suite asks for it (crates/effigy-gateway/src/proxy/performance.rs:44), so it carries no failure contract of its own.
One owner sequence for the private workspace up path, with the publication provider a typed injection boundary, but the module root is dead-code-allowed and carries feature-gated submodules.
Retires the selected session through ordinary store coordination and leaves the stop transition to recheck.
The one production owner sequence, with kernel custody not injectable.
One guarded apply that returns the exact owner on failure so the caller decides retention.
Publish, commit and select under the same reacquired owner; no Drop-based cleanup.
The one backend apply as an explicit process boundary, with a separate qualification strategy that still refuses ordinary production.
Recovers the private liveness slot only when the owner is proven absent; a live or unknown owner grants nothing.
Only names a temp path: the atomic publish it exists for is re-implemented at its two call sites, so one mechanism has three owners.

One fixed-shape privileged bind/pass boundary with peer identity, bounded I/O and exactly-two-descriptor custody; the authorised loopback range is now the crate's own compile-time pool rather than a repeated literal.
Single owner of the UDP resolver: typed question decode, one route lookup via the shared table, refusal for names it does not own.

One table and one fenced transaction, and an unobservable store is now a typed EndpointStoreRefusal (crates/effigy-gateway/src/endpoint_store/mod.rs:36) so a caller reports unproven absence instead of matching the message.
Typed crate-wide error boundary that keeps process-state-unknown distinct from not-running and carries the remedy in the message; the endpoint-store refusal kind now travels with the error.
Single owner of the trusted PID/identity pair: typed platform start identity, distinct Unknown/Mismatch/PermissionDenied probe, fail-closed records.
Crate wiring and re-exports only; the module list is the crate's public surface.

1826 product lines in one file own four separate mechanisms: the systemd user unit and its activation directory, the executable/CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE image rules, the bind-probe subprocess protocol, and directory custody with rewrite/restore compensation.
One adoption boundary: refuses root/elevated identities and any descriptor that is not the exact reserved loopback listener, closing every refusal exactly once.
The one poison-tolerant lock accessor for the always-on daemon.

The route table is the only record of loopback ownership, so there is no second assignment to reclaim; the pool size is now one named constant (crates/effigy-gateway/src/loopback.rs:21) with its sizing rationale.
One libproc fdinfo reader with pinned SDK offsets; a size or flavour mismatch is Unknown, never guessed.

The operator command still carries two lifecycle records (kernel run, plus the pre-0.15 PID file status arm) and a debug-only fixture guard inside product code; status is a label string and observations collapse to strings.
Static, probe-free port derivation: the same plan renders the same stack and a taken port is reported by the runtime bind failure; its digest now defers to effigy-core's one sha256 owner.
Validates a caller-owned private state root as a real owner-only directory and refuses symlinks and unexpected children.
Sound routing, streaming and refusal behaviour, but the internal /_effigy endpoints hand-build JSON that mirrors the typed Route and stats fields.
Route claims are one owner per domain, with an unknown target observation refusing takeover rather than guessing.
The file format and suffix validation are single-owner, but the per-route reconciler has no caller and the same file has two write paths.
Typed route snapshot; persistence is explicitly the endpoint Store's, so there is no second record here.
The serving loop is single-owner, but the PID/version-record and status/probe family duplicates what identity.rs and operator.rs already own, and it carries its own atomic publish.
The one administrator action, but 2,636 lines mix the receipt, the privileged session, the phase-line protocol and the native boot-job documents in one module.
Two typed values with one documented reader; deliberately not a process scanner.
Plain atomic counters, but the JSON shape is written by hand beside the fields it mirrors and the field names are duplicated as literals.
One reconcile loop that owns the alias listeners and their desired/active diff.

Certificates and the SNI resolver work, and crates/effigy-gateway/src/tls.rs:827 now proves the running gateway serves a route's own leaf; the CA-installed oracle still shells out and sniffs a tool's stderr text (crates/effigy-gateway/src/tls.rs:756).
One owner-only exclusive lock for up/down, with a waiting form only where certificate generation needs it.
The split landed: the file is now shared types plus src/runner/host_process.rs:45 and five sibling owners, and its lifecycle status/observation records are typed rather than string-coded.

One owner of a host process as a kernel run: admission, effects, stop report and settle all project the same journal, and the stop state is now typed (src/runner/host_process/kernel_run.rs:79) with a corrupt journal kept Unknown.
One owner of the published wait graph; the launcher is a seam so tests run the production graph, and four unused activation-trait methods were removed rather than left as surface.
A 55-line argument reshuffle with eight positional parameters whose only job is to call the plan resolver.
One typed parser for the managed verbs with named refusals for empty or unknown values.
Data shapes and the managed error boundary; a typed UI error still becomes a string bucket and the plan still carries `mode` as a raw string.

Plan resolution is single-owner and refuses invalid shapes, and delivered environment now travels beside its command rendering; the same facts are still passed both as a context struct and as a long parameter list.
One mode decision plus the plan renderer; nothing spawns.
One profile resolver with the available-profile list in its refusal.

Single owner of `{ task = ... }` reference parsing and resolution with good invalid/failed/missing-run distinctions, and a reference now carries a typed RenderedRun instead of a bare command string; nothing in the tree tests the parser directly.
Plain table/label rendering for the plan view, with the PTY rule stated in one place.
One command-rendering owner, and the delivered environment is now a typed field beside the command (crates/effigy-managed/src/run_spec.rs:62) instead of being re-parsed out of shell text.
One env accumulator over typed entries with a named refusal for an unknown key.
A three-line policy boundary over the run supervisor.
A nine-line legacy renderer with one caller, wrapping a step in a python3 timeout shim.
A 50-line dispatcher that keeps the one supervise entry and the settlement hooks for the run engine.
The run's front ends: one start path, typed engine events, and an owning client whose death stops the run.
A pure journal projection for status/logs/stop - no session file or PID is authority - though the projection re-derives facts from journal strings.

The run's only writer: admission, effects in order, workload custody and one settle, with stop causes typed; an unreadable stop mailbox now refuses (src/runner/managed_run/engine.rs:1300) instead of failing open.
The environment phase observes its own condition with a deadline that starts when the phase does, and a not-ready reason stays typed; nothing waits on a fixed timer.
Environment host processes as tabs: status comes from the owner journal and a generation-bound observation, never child log text.
One cursor over canonical bytes: offsets, replacement detection and bounded line framing in a single place.
The run's three effects and their one reversal, with unknown reasons kept and a borrowed environment retained.
One TUI front end over the same journal reads; shell tabs stay out of the run, quitting stops and settles, and an entry's exit is now carried as the typed code it recorded.
The client/supervisor message shapes, with the front end explicitly not influencing topology.
A second, shape-identical copy of the runner's task-routing error variants, kept in step by a mechanical From impl.
Crate wiring plus the one string-error adapter the manifest resolver callback requires.
Narrow routing-owned loader so manifest errors surface as RoutingError.
Single owner of explicit catalog membership, aliases and the origin-attributed refusals.
One selection strategy owner over typed CatalogSelectionMode; the evidence strings are presentation only.
Checkout paths, preflight and private host-process records: listener configurations and checkout paths are refused before any container or child startup can create an effect.
Host-process ordering and generation-bound dependency environments, with a typed DependencyRecord and an explicit wait outcome instead of a timeout guess.

Fail-fast JavaScript dependency drift before managed host processes start: it compares each declared dependency's installed copy with the checkout's own lock resolution and refuses by name, leaving an undeclared, unreadable or machine-linked package alone.

Host-process activation, replacement and readiness admission: each supervisor is a detached kernel run, a failing bring-up drops its owning pipes, and a listener that fails its own readiness withholds only its own route.
Resolved child environment, listener addresses and endpoint publication facts, with the CA trust variables filled only where the operator left them unset.
Lifecycle and journal observation for host-owned runs: the latest typed observation is the atomic publication, and a corrupt latest payload never falls back to an older snapshot.
Fenced stop requests, custody reports and listener route teardown, with the requester's wait derived from the supervisor's own stop window and residue named rather than dropped.

Listener generation readiness and route publication: one typed write carries a generation's address, route claim and child identity, and a failed generation reports the status that made the refusal terminal.
Activation and readiness observations for lifecycle callers, with a generation-matched barrier, bounded and redacted child-log tails, and no ANSI interpretation.
Admission, custody and restart policy for host-process generations: each cleanup step mints its own budget and a step that could not proceed reads as unavailable, never as an invalid request.
